key_insight: CFD Forge automates CFD case setup, execution, diagnosis, and reporting with an LLM, but uses deterministic physics checks—not the model—to decide whether results are accepted.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, more repeatable CFD workflows for design iteration and high-throughput studies while keeping acceptance decisions auditable and trustworthy.
method: LLM interprets the engineering request and proposes actions from a closed set.
OpenFOAM-based agent carries the case through geometry/case construction, meshing, solver execution, diagnostics, and reporting.
Registered deterministic checks evaluate flow-specific criteria and determine acceptance independently of the model.
evidence_signal: In 36 replayed simulation states with some altered diagnostics, the model accepted 12 of 13 detectable faults when judging without checks, but accepted none when CFD Forge’s checks controlled the verdicts.
watch_item: The framework depends on well-designed registered checks and robust diagnostics; if the checks are incomplete, failure modes may still slip through.
paper_title: CFD Forge: A Physics-Constrained Agentic Framework for Autonomous CFD
